title: A sharp 5/8 bound for Erdős Problem 865
abstract: Formalizes the resolution of Erdős Problem 865 on pairwise sums. For A ⊆ {1,…,N}, a pairwise-sum triple is a set of distinct a, b, c ∈ A with a+b, a+c, b+c all in A, and A is triple-free when it has none. The development proves that every triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, that any A exceeding this bound contains a triple, and — via the construction A = [M,2M] ∪ [4M,8M] for N = 8M — that the constant 5/8 is optimal, so f₃(N) = 5N/8 + O(1). The upper bound runs through a folded additive lemma over ℤ/mℤ (a four-set union bound) and a folding lemma, closed by strong induction on N.

informal.Erdos865.erdos865_upper_bound: Every triple-free set A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, i.e. |A| ≤ (5/8)·N + O(1).
informal.Erdos865.erdos865_contains_triple: Every A ⊆ [1,N] with 5·N + 53 < 8·|A| contains a pairwise-sum triple (the paper's Theorem 1.1 form).
informal.Erdos865.sharpness: For N = 8M with M ≥ 1 there is a triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] with 8·|A| = 5·N + 16, so the constant 5/8 is optimal.
